10.1002_aenm.70894: LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O 2 (NCM811)‐based lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are widely regarded as promising candidates for next‐generation high‐energy‐density systems. However, under high‐temperature and high‐voltage conditions, severe interfacial side reactions between the electrolyte and electrodes are inevitably triggered, substantially impeding the practical development of LMBs. Herein, a mechanically and thermally robust LiF/LiB x O y ‐rich CEI on NCM811 via synergistic regulation of a LiBF 4 /LiDFOB dual‐salt electrolyte and a functional boron‐containing additive 2,4,6‐tris(3,4,5‐trifluorophenyl)boroxin (TTFPB) is rationally constructed. The LiBF 4 /LiDFOB dual‐salt system enhances electrolyte thermal and oxidative stability, while TTFPB reconstructs the Li + solvation structure by selectively excluding DFOB − from the primary solvation sheath and enriching BF 4 − coordination, thereby inducing an anion‐rich solvation structure. Meanwhile, TTFPB/DFOB − species preferentially decompose at the cathode interphase, generating a uniform and mechanically robust LiF/LiB x O y ‐rich CEI. This stabilized interphase effectively suppresses continuous electrolyte decomposition and mitigates transition‐metals ions (TMs) dissolution, also alleviates cathode phase transitions. Consequently, Li||NCM811 batteries with this electrolyte deliver 80.70% capacity retention after 350 cycles at 4.5 V. Notably, even under extreme operating conditions at 4.5 V and 80°C, the batteries retain 87.50% of their initial capacity after 100 cycles.
10.1002_smll.75049: Scandium ion, Sc 3+ , was introduced into O3‐Na[Ni 1/2 Mn 1/2 ]O 2 either by bulk doping or by surface coating. We prepared O3‐type Na[(Ni II 1/2 Mn IV 1/2 ) 1‐ x Sc III x ]O 2 and Sc 2 O 3 ‐coated Na[Ni 1/2 Mn 1/2 ]O 2, and the resulting materials were systematically compared for application to a rechargeable battery. Electrochemical evaluation revealed that both strategies remarkably improved cycling performance in Na half‐cells, increasing the capacity retention after 100 cycles from 18.6% to 67.8% for Sc‐doped and to 75.4% for Sc‐coated samples, and enabled sustained long‐term operation for over 300 cycles in sodium‐ion cells. We found the two strategies enhanced cycling performance through distinct mechanisms. The bulk doping, inducing a structural Na‐pillar between two MeO 2 slabs (Me = Ni, Mn, Sc), stabilizes the lattice by attracting local Na + with redox‐inactive Sc 3+ and suppressing rapid lattice shrinkage during sodium extraction. Furthermore, the discharge potential can be smoothened by suppressing the unwanted O’3 phase, which is validated by both ex situ XRD and DFT calculations. The coating appears to improve interfacial stability, possibly by suppressing transition‐metal dissolution. These findings clarify the distinct contributions of bulk Sc doping and Sc‐based surface modification to the cycling stability of O3‐Na[Ni 1/2 Mn 1/2 ]O 2 and suggest that separate optimization of bulk and interfacial modifications is a promising strategy for developing more durable Na‐layered oxide cathodes.
10.1016_j.electacta.2026.148522: MXenes are among the 2D materials that have been widely used in the development of electrochemical sensors, with applications in various fields, including pharmaceutical analysis. MXene-based (bio)sensors were most frequently applied to the detection of antibiotics and anticancer drugs, primarily through the catalytic oxidation of phenolic groups of drugs at suitable applied potentials. The roles and functionalities of MXenes in electrochemical (bio)sensors for drug analysis are discussed, focusing on their catalytic activity, large surface area, and abundant anchoring sites. However, recent studies show that pristine MXenes lack the capability to develop highly sensitive electrochemical sensors for drug analysis, necessitating the introduction of new functionalities through incorporation with nanoparticles, nanotubes, graphene, and metal-organic frameworks forming multifunctional composite materials. The complex synthesis process, which often involves the use of toxic hydrofluoric acid (HF), along with the susceptibility of MXenes to oxidation, represents the primary challenges in developing MXene-based electrochemical sensors. This work reviews advances in the development of MXene-based sensors for pharmaceutical analysis during the period of 2019 – 2025. It provides a critical assessment of the MXene-based sensor technology and reviews the achieved performance in pharmaceutical applications. Furthermore, it highlights future research directions that may facilitate a broader adoption of MXenes in electrochemical sensors for pharmaceutical analysis and other application areas.
10.1016_j.est.2026.121989: This document presents the development of two mathematical models for an industrial lithium battery. For this purpose, a 48 V , 3500 Wh Li–FePO4 battery from the Pylontech brand was used. This battery operates within a photovoltaic system with energy storage installed at the laboratory of the “Centro de Energias Renovables y Uso Racional de la Energia de la Universidad Nacional de Ingenieria” (Center for Renewable Energy and Rational Use of Energy of the National University of Engineering), located in Lima, Peru. The mathematical models include the dynamic and thermal models of the lithium battery. The electrical behavior observed in the battery is not solely attributed to the battery as an electrochemical element but is also influenced by the power system that connects it to the photovoltaic system, the control system and the internal instrumentation. The developed models are validated using experimental data from the electrical response of the battery when the photovoltaic system operates under a specific photovoltaic production and consumption profile. Additionally, it is observed that noise in the current signal increases as its value decreases. Therefore, to achieve results with acceptable precision, two algorithms were implemented for smoothing the current signal, which serves as an input variable for the developed models. A total of 96% of the calculated NRMSE values fall below 5%, encompassing comparisons between measured and simulated voltage, current, and power of the battery under the various operating conditions evaluated, which provides clear evidence of the strong performance of the proposed models.
10.1021_acscatal.6c04010: Ir-based anodes for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) often degrade when lattice oxygen participates in acidic OER, accelerating Ir dissolution. Here, we engineer the interfacial water microenvironment by alloying Au with low-crystallinity Ir nanoclusters on TiO2 (IrAu0.12@TiO2). The Ir-Au work-function mismatch induces interfacial electronic polarization, strengthens metal–water interactions, facilitates rapid water activation, and reorganizes the hydrogen (H)-bond network to enrich weakly H-bonded (“free”) H2O at active sites. Operando Raman spectroscopy captures, at lower potentials, the accelerated conversion of H-bonded water into free-H2O, while 18O differential electrochemical mass spectrometry confirms markedly suppressed lattice-oxygen contributions from the surface oxide layer, indicating a shift from the LOM (lattice oxygen mechanism) to the AEM (adsorbate evolution mechanism)-dominated pathway. Kinetic isotope effects, Tafel-isotope analyses, and thermodynamic–kinetic simulations further reveal lowered barriers for water dissociation and accelerated proton-coupled electron transfer. Consequently, IrAu0.12@TiO2 delivers 10 mA cm–2 at 230 mV and a mass activity of 633.7 A gIr–1 at 275 mV and sustains PEMWE operation for 510 h at 1 A cm–2 with 98.2% retention. This work highlights interfacial water microenvironment engineering as a generalizable route to couple high activity with long-term durability in acidic OER electrocatalysts for PEMWE anodes.
